items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: Do you remember who the two were? Yeah. We had Zeb, Neely, times like that, you know. Georgey Boy and George Lewis.

ctx.x: He was really great blues man. Who did Chris have in his band, if you'd say so?

Oh, I had George Lewis. At various times they would play together a while and Georgey Boy, certainly I, Neely Bones, at certain times they would have two jobs and split up. I saw him have jobs in using two clarinet players in the band. Do you remember who the two were? Yeah. We had Zeb, Neely, times like that, you know. Georgey Boy and George Lewis. Mostly it would be Tyne, like maybe perhaps he was short of a man, a trombone player, or either a bass player. It must have sounded good. It must have sounded good.…
Albert's system, Albert's system, Albert's system, no Barum system.

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: I never heard anybody do that until about 1945, when once Jim Robinson and George Lewis.

ctx.x: And Pork Chop Rag, he was real great on that. High Society, ice cream, he really can play those numbers. He played ice cream too?
Oh yeah, all those numbers, yeah. I never heard anybody do that until about 1945, when once Jim Robinson and George Lewis. Oh yeah, that's... They played it way back though.

Yeah, they did, yeah, they played that way back. Really, he was a real great musician. And I played with Silly Stamp Band, made up a band, not our, he made the band up. This was in around, last of 41. He had, things had gotten bad and he had broke up his band. He didn't have any band, Silly Stamp, Papa Silly Stamp.
